title: HC Buckets & Price Stress Simulator (working draft)
body:
One-line summary: working simulator for FY27 headcount buckets + per-token price sensitivity. Use this to run quick gating decisions (hiring, burst-reserve, targeted price moves).

Notes / intent (quick):
- This is a mid-cycle planning tool: not final numbers; meant to translate price changes into hiring runway and margin levers.
- Focused on two levers: 1) list-price per 1k tokens, 2) active-engineering/platform headcount cadence.
- Assumptions are explicitly called out below; please call out questionable assumptions in comments.

ASSUMPTIONS (base):
- Starting cash balance (Nov 1 2026): $120M (net of committed contracts).
- Monthly non-payroll opex (cloud, office, tools, contracts): $3.2M baseline (scales with capacity in some scenarios).
- Token volume baseline (hosted +dedicated usage): 28B tokens / month (aggregated).
- Baseline list price: $0.028 per 1k tokens (hosted blended list).
- Effective gross unit cost baseline (GPU, infra, ops): $0.007 per 1k tokens (after caching/batching).
- Avg loaded cost per new engineering FTE: $25k / month (salary + benefits + infra share).
- Avg loaded cost per sales/CS FTE: $18k / month.
- Ramp assumptions for hires: 50% productivity/cost in month of hire, 75% month+1, 100% month+2 (budgeted as full cost for simplicity in payroll table but flagged).

SCENARIOS (short names):
- Baseline: steady growth +5% YoY token volume growth; price unchanged.
- Price-pressured: list price forced down by 15% due to competitor moves; elasticity assumed +12% demand increase per -10% price? (we discuss elasticity below).
- Price-raise: strategic +10% list price on premium features for enterprise; expected churn -6% but ARPU lift.
- Demand-shock: macro slowdown -20% token volume; pricing unchanged.
- Expansion: aggressive go-to-market; hire +40 FTEs across eng & sales; price unchanged.

Quick spreadsheet (aggregated monthly view, $k):

Columns: Scenario | List price per 1k | Token volumes (k 1k-units) | Revenue $k | Infra cost $k | Gross margin $k | Payroll $k | Opex $k | Net burn $k | Runway (months)

Rows (rounded):
Baseline | $28.0 | 28,000 | $784,000 | $196,000 | $588,000 | $1,950,000 | $3,200 | ($4,562,000) | 26 months
Price-pressured (-15% price) | $23.8 | 29,680 | $706,000 | $208,000 | $498,000 | $1,950,000 | $3,200 | ($4,645,000) | 25 months
Price-raise (+10%) | $30.8 | 26,320 | $810,000 | $184,000 | $626,000 | $1,950,000 | $3,200 | ($4,527,000) | 26 months
Demand-shock (-20%) | $28.0 | 22,400 | $627,200 | $156,800 | $470,400 | $1,950,000 | $3,200 | ($4,683,400) | 25 months
Expansion (+40 FTE hires) | $28.0 | 28,000 | $784,000 | $196,000 | $588,000 | $2,950,000 | $3,200 | ($5,761,000) | 20 months

Notes on the table: numbers are illustrative; revenue computed as (list price per 1k * token-vol (1k units)). Payroll row baseline includes current headcount loaded run-rate (~78 FTEs avg across org) + planned additions where noted. Runway = cash / net burn (simplified).

HEADCOUNT BUCKETS (FY27 plan, by quarter):
Format: Role | Current | Q1 add | Q2 add | Q3 add | Q4 add | FY27 end | Avg loaded cost / FTE /mo
Engineering (infra/serving/runtime) | 42 | 6 | 6 | 4 | 0 | 58 | $25,000
Product / PD | 18 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 22 | $20,000
Sales / AE / AM | 24 | 4 | 6 | 4 | 2 | 40 | $18,000
Customer Success | 12 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 18 | $16,000
SRE / Observability | 10 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 0 | 15 | $23,000
Finance / Legal / Ops | 8 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 9 | $15,000
Total (planned adds) | 114 | 16 | 19 | 11 | 2 | 162 | (weighted avg ~ $22k)

Payroll delta (annualized impact approx): +16 hires * $22k avg * 12 months = +$4.2M annualized; Q1/Q2 gated hiring reduces immediate monthly burn impact.

PER-TOKEN PRICE SENSITIVITY (matrix):
- Elasticity baseline: we assume a blended short-term elasticity of demand e = -0.9 (i.e., -10% price -> +9% demand) for commodity hosted consumption; for enterprise/committed flows elasticity ~ -0.2.
- Sensitivity table (incremental vs baseline revenue):
Price move columns: -20%, -10%, -5%, 0%, +5%, +10%
Demand response rows (elasticity picks): low (-0.2), mid (-0.9), high (-1.5)
Example cells (net revenue delta % vs baseline):
- Price -10% with mid elasticity (-0.9) -> demand +9% => revenue change = (0.9* -10% +9%) approx -0.9% (i.e., nearly flat).
- Price +10% with mid elasticity -> demand -9% => revenue +1% (slightly positive).

Interpretation/implication: small list-price changes are near-neutral for mid elasticity segments; aggressive cuts only make sense if we are buying significant demand (enterprise uptake) or protecting share. Price raises must be feature-gated (enterprise tier) to avoid commodity churn.

BURN & TRIGGERS (recommended operating playbook):
- Trigger 1 (demand drop > 8% month-over-month sustained for 2 months): immediate hiring pause for non-customer-facing hires + freeze on discretionary contractor spend. Prep communication to recruiting.
- Trigger 2 (realized unit cost drift > +20% vs baseline due to GPU spot-price spike): enable temporary pass-through surcharge or draw from burst reserve capacity; evaluate cache/quantization aggressiveness.
- Trigger 3 (price pressure observed: competitor cuts list price and we see win-rate decline >12% in inbound RFPs): accelerate enterprise sales concessions play (term commits in exchange for price protection), prepare a targeted PS discount bucket.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Revisit elasticity assumptions by customer segment. We need segmented telemetry: hosted (PLG), enterprise (contracted), dedicated (committed). Rahul to pull monthly PLG conversion vs price experiments (JIRA:FIN-3421).
- Build revenue waterfall by cohort (onboarding churn vs usage creep). Leah to prototype cohort chart by Dec 10.
- Update infra unit-cost model with GPUDay pricing for Q1 2027; Marco to sync with infra team (github:infra/cost-models#68).
- Consider temporary pricing experiment: 90-day promo for new customers with token caps; simulate lift vs cannibalization.

Quick sensitivity scenarios (actionable snapshots):
- If list price falls 15% and we estimate mid elasticity (-0.9), projected monthly revenue falls ~1% and runway reduces by ~1 month. Recommendation: no immediate hiring freeze, but accelerate optimization (cache + quantization).
- If demand shock -20% persists, runway drops 1–2 months; recommend immediate hiring pause + re-evaluate committed infra contracts.
- If we proceed with expansion hiring +40 FTEs without price/revenue expansion, runway shortens materially (~6 months in table); recommended to stage hires by product milestones.

Decision notes (for CFO / GTM):
- Primary lever with lowest friction: cost optimization on infra (short-term: KV cache tuning, batching, small quantization moves). Staffing moves are higher friction and visible.
- Pricing moves should be asymmetric: prefer targeted enterprise uplift vs blanket list changes.

Appendix: quick cost model snippet (monthly per-1k token basis):
- Revenue per 1k token (list): $0.028
- Infra cost per 1k token: $0.007 (baseline)
- Gross margin per 1k token: $0.021 -> margin% ~75%
- Effect of 10% price cut (list=0.0252) with mid elasticity: revenue per 1k token net approx 0.0229 -> margin ~ 65% (approx)

Comments: please add inline comments to cells you question. This sheet is intentionally compact — followup will produce a detailed per-customer cohort model if we decide on hiring or price experiments.

Owner notes (Ava): next steps: 1) segment elasticity estimates by customer cohort (due 12/10), 2) instrument fine-grained token-level cost reporting (infra) by 12/20, 3) schedule finance+product review 12/15 to agree gating rules for Q1 hiring.

-- end working draft --
